newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway nationwide wage talks break down.
newsitem.headline: Norway nationwide wage talks break down.

text.p: Nationwide wage talks between Norwegian workers and management broke down on Wednesday, paving the way for mediation due to begin next month, officials said.
The breakdown followed remarks by Central Bank Governor Kjell Storvik earlier in the day that the inflation outlook now depended partly on the outcome of wage negotiations in the labour market.
The Trade Union Confederation (LO) said it broke off talks with the Confederation of Trade and Industry (NHO) because the latter refused to accept early retirement for some workers.
"Because of this it was impossible for the confederation of trade unions to carry on the talks," said LO in a statement.

The parties also disagreed on whether the talks, which are supplementary to the major round of biennial central wage talks which took place last year, entitled some local groups to negotiate extra wage increases on a central basis.
NHO said in a statement that last year's central wage talks meant real term wage growth of nearly three percent, helping to fuel inflation.

"The wage hikes of 1996 will have a considerable effect on wage growth in 1997. This effect -- the overhang -- will together with an expected wage drift in 1997 and the strengthened crown lead to a considerable growth in real wages," NHO said.

"At the same time the competitive edge of Norwegian companies is weakening. NHO therefore feels that there is no room for wage increases in the supplementary talks in 1997 for groups entitled to local negotiations," it said.
The talks broke down after five days.
NHO officials said state mediation would begin on April 1 with a deadline set for April 7.
A series of strikes hurting the offshore and manufacturing industries marred Norway's labour scene last year after state-led mediation failed to bring parties together in time.
